```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}
```

```{r key-helpers, include=FALSE}
ans_col <- rgb(200, 0, 130, maxColorValue = 255)
# redraws blank_table() so cells flagged TRUE in `ans` use the answer color
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, bold_rows = integer(0), ans = NULL) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      is_ans <- !is.null(ans) && isTRUE(ans[[i]][[j]])
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val, cex = cex,
                                    font = if (i %in% bold_rows) 2 else 1,
                                    col = if (is_ans) ans_col else "black")
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}
```

\ans{\textbf{Answer key.} Answers are in magenta.}


**NRES 746, Week 6, Lecture 2: Find the Bugs**


**Instructions:** Work alone for about 3 minutes, then compare with a
neighbor. Keep laptops closed.

## The code

Here are two short functions, possibly written with AI help. The first
comes from today's live-coding problem (finishing Lab 4's toad
monitoring design).

- `detect_prob(k)`: one person-day of searching detects an animal with
  probability `pobs`, so `k` person-days should detect it with
  probability $1 - (1 - p_{obs})^k$.
- `sim_detect(R)`: should simulate `R` surveys of a site where the frog
  from Lab 5 is present (3 visits per survey, detection probability
  0.4 per visit) and return the fraction of surveys with at least one
  detection.

Each function below contains **exactly one bug**. Both run without an
error, but give wrong answers.

```{r buggy-code, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
detect_prob <- function(k, pobs = 0.02) {
  1 - pobs^k
}

sim_detect <- function(R = 1000, visits = 3, p = 0.4) {
  detected <- logical(R)
  for (i in seq_len(R)) {
    n_det <- rbinom(1, size = visits, prob = p)
    detected <- n_det > 0
  }
  mean(detected)
}
```

## Part 1: Find and fix (individual, ~3 min)

For each function, circle the bug on the code above, write the
corrected line, and say what would go wrong if you ran the buggy
version.

**1a.** `detect_prob()`

\ans{Fix: \texttt{1 - (1 - pobs)\^{}k}. The buggy version, $1 - p_{obs}^k$, returns nearly 1 for any effort (e.g. 0.9996 for $k = 2$), so detection looks almost certain.}

**1b.** `sim_detect()`

\ans{Fix: \texttt{detected[i] <- n\_det > 0}. The buggy version overwrites the whole vector every survey, so it returns only the last survey's result (exactly 0 or 1).}

## Part 2: Catch it next time (with a neighbor, ~2 min)

**2.** For one of the bugs, what quick check (one line of code and the
answer you'd expect) would have caught it?

\ans{E.g. \texttt{detect\_prob(1)} should return 0.02 (one day = \texttt{pobs}); or \texttt{sim\_detect()} should be near $1 - 0.6^3 = 0.784$, never exactly 0 or 1.}
